worked: Single, age 60. IRA, employer plan and private annuity share one 6,000 for the person (all are Lines 4b and 5b), and income is under the limit. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages 16,000.00 + pensions 1,000.00 + IRA distributions 4,000.00 + employer plan distributions 3,000.00 = 24,000.00. Federal taxable income = 24,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 8,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form MO-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 24,000.00. Line 2 additions 0.00. Line 3 total income 24,000.00. Line 4 subtractions 0.00. Line 6 Missouri adjusted gross income 24,000.00 - 0.00 = 24,000.00. Section B: Line 1 24,000.00; Line 2 0.00; Line 3 24,000.00; Line 4 25,000.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 6Y 8,000.00, Line 7Y 6,000.00; Line 8 6,000.00; Line 9 6,000.00. Form MO-1040 Line 8 pension and Social Security exemption 6,000.00. Lines 9-13 federal income tax deduction not applied (not modelled; the household's federal tax is not an input). Line 14 standard deduction 15,750.00. Line 26 subtotal 24,000.00 - 6,000.00 - 15,750.00 = 2,250.00. Line 29 taxable income 2,250.00. Tax by the bands (0% to 1,313): 2% x 937.00 = 18.74; total 18.74 = 18.74. The chart and Tax Calculation Worksheet (instructions p21) round to the dollar and give 19; expected keeps the bands. state_agi (after every relief, as the check format defines it) = Line 6 24,000.00 - Line 8 6,000.00 = 18,000.00; the form's Missouri AGI is Line 6, 24,000.00.
accepted_approximations: The chart's cumulative amounts are rounded to whole dollars and the tax to the nearest dollar; the bands here do neither.
The federal income tax deduction is not applied (not_modelled).
